items.claim: The row discloses the weaker of the two byte-parallels available to it, misstates the difference at the site it does disclose, and leaves unnamed the source block it reuses - byte-identical in 16 of 19 words at its middle verse - whose extent coincides exactly with this span.
items.evidence: Re-collation: both splices reach byte tier at their cited refs. The disclosed relation fails on the bytes. oshb:Jer.50.43 closes צָרָה֙ הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְהוּ חִ֖יל כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה; oshb:Jer.49.24 closes צָרָ֧ה וַחֲבָלִ֛ים אֲחָזַ֖תָּה כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה. Word for word the two share exactly one form, כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה: the seizing verb is a different root at each site, 49:24 inserts a second noun, and 49:24 carries no counterpart to 50:43's חִ֖יל (0 occurrences in that verse). The row states the difference as the verb of onset, heard against has grown feeble - those are the two verses' opening verbs, standing outside the idiom altogether, so the stated difference is not the difference the bytes carry; and 'near match' ships with no tier. Meanwhile the byte-nearest relation goes unnamed: this span reproduces oshb:Jer.6.22-Jer.6.24. oshb:Jer.50.42 stands byte-identical to oshb:Jer.6.23 in 16 of its 19 words, the substantive substitution being בַּת בָּבֶֽל for בַּת צִיּֽוֹן; oshb:Jer.6.24 closes צָרָה֙ הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְנוּ חִ֖יל כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה, differing from 50:43's idiom in the verb's pronominal suffix alone. That reuse begins and ends exactly at this row's own two seams, so disclosing it would have corroborated the cut - naming a one-word parallel in its place inverts the evidence weight, and neither the block nor the divergence detail reaches the evidence refs.
tier_citations: byte (both row splices re-collated at their cited refs)

items.claim: The grammatical test used to reject a cut at 50:44|50:45 is byte-false, the block relation that would actually carry the rejection is unstated, and the row's one mark citation drops its witness disclosure.
items.evidence: Re-collation: all three splices reach byte tier, and the note handling at oshb:Jer.50.44 is correct - the source carries both forms inside the verse, ארוצם אֲרִיצֵם֙, one note in the single-witness inventory, with the plural object suffix standing against the singular at oshb:Jer.49.19 on the pointed bytes. The rejection warrant does not hold. It asserts that the sentence begun in the simile continues grammatically past the verse boundary; but oshb:Jer.50.44 ends לְפָנָֽי, completing its rhetorical question at the verse end, and oshb:Jer.50.45 opens לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ, a fresh imperative clause introduced by therefore. The link is inferential, not a continuing sentence, so the test said to kill the split never runs. What would carry it is unstated: 50:44-45 travels as a block with 49:19-20 (23 of 28 and 20 of 24 words byte-identical), whereas oshb:Jer.50.46 shares a single word with oshb:Jer.49.21 - so calling all three verses one reprise of that template overstates the third. Undisclosed counter-pressure: the parallel Edom sequence carries a setumah immediately after its lion verse at oshb:Jer.49.19 - tier-3, single witness, weak, offered only as corroboration that the tradition divided there, never as a driver. Finally the row's closing mark is correctly typed setumah in the inventory but is cited as a bare Jer.50.46, with no witness prefix and no single-witness disclosure, unlike the mark citations at 51:14, 51:19 and 51:24.
tier_citations: ketiv/qere, single-witness inventory plus verse bytes

items.claim: The span carries an undisclosed ketiv/qere at 51:3, in the very verse the row argues from, and the row's Hebrew engagement stops short of the form its own onset claim rests on.
items.evidence: Verified sound first: both splices reach byte tier; the chapter's formula digit is right (sweep: 4 verses - 51:1, 51:33, 51:36, 51:58), all four divine report with no human mouth intervening, so the frame-ownership reasoning stands; and treating the boundary at 50:46|51:1 as a row seam inside a parent that continues is correct. The disclosure fails. oshb:Jer.51.3 carries a ketiv/qere note (one, single-witness inventory), and the doubling is visible in the verse bytes themselves - אֶֽל יִדְרֹ֤ךְ ידרך הַדֹּרֵךְ֙, the verb standing twice, once pointed and once bare. The row argues from that verse's content, the commissioned archers, and says nothing about the note, while the notes falling at oshb:Jer.51.9 and oshb:Jer.51.13 are each disclosed where they fall; in an inventory of 141 notes over 124 verses a span-touching note is an unconditional disclosure, and the asymmetry here sits inside one stretch. Two smaller byte gaps: the English attached to the 51:5 splice runs past it to cover וִֽיהוּדָה֙ מֵֽאֱלֹהָ֔יו, which the splice does not contain; and the cipher name at oshb:Jer.51.1, לֵ֣ב קָמָ֑י, is left wholly unengaged although the onset argument sits on that verse.
tier_citations: ketiv/qere, single-witness inventory plus verse bytes

items.claim: The two-speaker reading inside 51:9-10 is carried by the English punctuation rather than by anything the Hebrew marks.
items.evidence: Verified sound first: the 51:6 splice reaches byte tier, 51:6 is a genuine verse-initial imperative onset, refusing to treat the embedded voice as a fresh frame-owner is the right call under this book's formula-ownership hazard, and the note claim at oshb:Jer.51.9 is byte-true - the verse opens רפאנו רִפִּ֣ינוּ, a healing-verb spelling variant standing first in the verse. The speaker split does not hold on the bytes. The row separates an embedded foreign voice at 51:9 from the returning exiles' own words at 51:10, but oshb:Jer.51.9 and oshb:Jer.51.10 run continuously in the first person plural with no speech frame between them - five first-person-plural forms across the two verses, רִפִּ֣ינוּ and וְנֵלֵ֖ךְ at 51:9, צִדְקֹתֵ֑ינוּ, וּנְסַפְּרָ֣ה and אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ at 51:10 - and the source marks no change of mouth. What separates them is the nested single quotation the English rendering opens at web:Jer.51.10 and not at web:Jer.51.9: modern punctuation, tier-4, never evidence in either direction. Two lesser points: the note claim quotes no Hebrew form and credits the identification to the inventory, which supplies only the count, while the position and the variant are readable only in the verse bytes; and the English attached to the 51:6 splice runs past it to cover וּמַלְּטוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ.
tier_citations: ketiv/qere, single-witness inventory count plus verse bytes
tier-4 (modern quotation punctuation in the English rendering)

items.claim: The stated seam driver does not separate this cut from two uncut imperative clusters in the same stretch, and a byte-true stirring-verb thread crossing three adjacent row onsets goes undisclosed.
items.evidence: Verified sound first: both splices reach byte tier, the oath gloss matches its splice exactly, the setumah at oshb:Jer.51.14 is correctly typed and single-witness disclosed, the note at oshb:Jer.51.13 is correctly counted at one, and the direct-address reading is supportable from the pointed second-feminine forms שֹׁכַנְתְּ֙ and קִצֵּ֖ךְ אַמַּ֥ת בִּצְעֵֽךְ - a pointed-byte reading, since the English does not distinguish the form and the row quotes neither. Two byte problems. First, discourse-imperative onset as stated fits oshb:Jer.51.8 הֵילִ֣ילוּ עָלֶ֗יהָ קְח֤וּ and oshb:Jer.51.12 שְׂאוּ נֵ֗ס equally well, and neither is cut; what actually separates 51:6 and 51:11 from those is verse-initial position, which the row never names, so the driver as written does not discriminate its own seam. Second, this row's onset verse carries הֵעִ֣יר יְהוָ֗ה, the same stirring root standing at the two adjacent row onsets - הִנְנִי֙ מֵעִ֣יר at oshb:Jer.51.1 and the niphal in וּמְלָכִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים יֵעֹ֖רוּ at oshb:Jer.50.41, with a further occurrence at oshb:Jer.50.9 - a shared-root thread crossing three row seams that no row in this stretch discloses. Both witnesses render the class alike, so the identification rests on the pointed bytes plus both renderings; no book-wide digit is offered for it, because the unpointed skeleton of this root collides with the noun for city and a bare substring sweep would be a blended count. Lesser: the English attached to the 51:11 splice covers a second imperative, מִלְא֣וּ הַשְּׁלָטִים֒, that the splice does not contain, and the comparison to a denser cluster later in the chapter carries no verse and no digit (the site is oshb:Jer.51.34, five notes).
tier_citations: pointed-byte form reading (no morphology layer staged; English does not distinguish)

items.claim: All three Hebrew splices in the row are glossed with clauses they do not contain, and the doxology-twin claim ships untiered against a text that diverges in three of its five verse pairs.
items.evidence: All three splices reach byte tier at their cited refs, and each English string attached to them is verbatim, so a verbatim check passes; the failure is the pairing, three times out of three. At oshb:Jer.51.15 the splice is עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֨רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ, rendered “He has made the earth by his power” (web:Jer.51.15), while the English attached is “He has established the world by his wisdom” (web:Jer.51.15), which renders מֵכִ֥ין תֵּבֵ֖ל בְּחָכְמָת֑וֹ. At oshb:Jer.51.16 the splice is לְק֨וֹל תִּתּ֜וֹ, rendered “When he utters his voice” (web:Jer.51.16), while the English attached is “there is a roar of waters in the heavens” (web:Jer.51.16), which renders הֲמ֥וֹן מַ֨יִם֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם - precisely the words the row's own argument says are not the at-the-sound phrase. At oshb:Jer.51.19 the splice is יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ, rendered “Yahweh of Armies is his name” (web:Jer.51.19), while the English attached is “The portion of Jacob is not like these” (web:Jer.51.19), which renders לֹֽא כְאֵ֜לֶּה חֵ֣לֶק יַעֲק֗וֹב at the far end of the verse. Second defect: the doxology relation is asserted as a twin with no tier. On the bytes oshb:Jer.51.15 stands byte-identical to oshb:Jer.10.12 and oshb:Jer.51.18 to oshb:Jer.10.15, but 51:16, 51:17 and 51:19 all diverge - oshb:Jer.51.19 reads Jacob plene, יַעֲק֗וֹב, against defective יַעֲקֹ֗ב at oshb:Jer.10.16, a live mater class inside this row's own span, and reads וְשֵׁ֖בֶט נַחֲלָת֑וֹ where 10:16 reads וְיִ֨שְׂרָאֵ֔ל שֵׁ֖בֶט נַֽחֲלָת֑וֹ. A row that names the relation, sits at high confidence and carries no frontier flag owes those divergences. Sound and worth keeping: the false lamed-header call at 51:16 is correct, and the shift from second-person address to third-person hymn is byte-marked.

items.claim: The refrain digit is false under both units, and the closing splice is glossed with the clause standing before it.
items.evidence: Both splices reach byte tier. The digit fails. The row calls the break-in-pieces refrain fivefold; on the bytes the form וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ stands nine times across oshb:Jer.51.20-Jer.51.23, distributed one, two, three, three - nine occurrences over four verses. Five is the book-wide verse count of that form (sweep: 5 verses - 51:20, 51:21, 51:22, 51:23 and oshb:Jer.13.14), a figure that includes a site outside this block and outside the nations material entirely; the row's claim names no unit and carries no sweep citation, so it is wrong under the token reading, wrong under the in-span verse reading, and right only for a book-wide count it does not mean. Gloss pairing fails at the close: the splice at oshb:Jer.51.24 is נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה, rendered “says Yahweh” (web:Jer.51.24), while the English attached is “all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight” (web:Jer.51.24), which renders אֵ֧ת כָּל רָעָתָ֛ם אֲשֶׁר עָשׂ֥וּ בְצִיּ֖וֹן לְעֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם, the clause immediately before it; and the English on the 51:20 splice מַפֵּץ אַתָּ֣ה לִ֔י runs past it to cover כְּלֵ֖י מִלְחָמָ֑ה. Verified sound: the addressee shift at 51:20 is marked in the pointed bytes by second-masculine אַתָּ֣ה and בְךָ֙ against the second-feminine address to Babylon at oshb:Jer.51.13 - a pointed-byte reading, since the English does not distinguish; oshb:Jer.51.24 continues the same first-person chain that runs through 51:20-23, so including it is right; the setumah at 51:24 is correctly typed and disclosed; and reading the postpositive formula as closure corroboration is right, since a fresh onset does follow at oshb:Jer.51.25.
tier_citations: skeleton sweep, verse and token units (9 tokens over 4 verses in span; 5 verses book-wide)
pointed-byte form reading (English does not distinguish)
